sources.entry: ClipFlow - Free clipboard history manager with terminal-style navigation. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/praneeth552/clipflow) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
ClipFlow - Clipboard history manager for macOS with terminal-style navigation, image previews, and cursor-following popup.

summary.one_liner: ClipFlow is a free, open-source clipboard history manager for macOS that lets you browse recent copies with terminal-style up/down keys from a cursor-following popup.
summary.what_it_does: The app saves the last 50 clipboard items, including text and images, and shows them in a popup that appears above the cursor. You move through the history with the up and down arrow keys, as you would through shell history, and press Enter or release Cmd to paste the selected item. Cmd+Shift+Delete removes the current item, and pasted items move to the top of the list. The popup shows image thumbnails, works across multiple monitors, and is non-focusable so it does not interrupt typing. The README says history is kept only in memory and clears when the app quits, and that the app makes no network connections. Persistent history, configurable history size, shortcut customization, search, and pinning are listed as roadmap items, not current features.
use_cases: recall recently copied text or images on a Mac
paste an earlier clipboard item without re-copying it
replace missing clipboard history on macOS
private clipboard manager that works offline
how_to_run: Download ClipFlow-1.0.2.dmg from Releases, drag ClipFlow.app to Applications, and open it
Grant Accessibility permission in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility
Or install with Homebrew: brew tap praneeth552/clipflow && brew install --cask clipflow
Or build from source: git clone the repo, cd clipflow/ClipFlowApp, run ./build.sh
Quick compile: swiftc -o ClipFlow ClipFlowApp.swift -framework AppKit -framework Carbon
notable: Terminal-style up/down navigation through clipboard history
Recently used items move to the top of the list after pasting
Cursor-following, non-focusable popup with image previews
No network access and history stays local in memory, cleared on quit
Build script produces a .app bundle and DMG installer
caveats: Requires macOS 12 or later and Accessibility permission for global hotkeys
Not notarized, so macOS shows an 'unidentified developer' warning on first launch; a right-click Open workaround is needed
History is not persisted and is lost when the app quits; search, pinning, and configurable shortcuts are roadmap items only
